draft.title: Megafauna and changing climate
card: Megafauna means giant animals. Australia once had many, such as Diprotodon, a plant-eating marsupial about the size of a small car.
The first peoples of Australia lived alongside megafauna. Both were in Australia for a long time, so people and these animals shared the land.
Over thousands of years the climate became drier in many places. Lakes and rivers shrank, so water and food were found in different places.
Megafauna later died out. Historians and scientists still study why, and they look at evidence about climate change and about people.
draft.remember: Megafauna shared the land with the first peoples, then died out as the climate dried.

a.q: What does the evidence in this card say about Diprotodon and the first peoples of Australia?
opts: They lived in Australia at the same time
They never lived in the same part of Australia
Diprotodon arrived after the first peoples left
Diprotodon was a hunter of the first peoples
a.why: The card says people lived alongside megafauna, so their time in Australia overlapped. Diprotodon was a plant-eating animal, so it did not hunt people.

b.q: Over thousands of years, the climate in a region of Australia became drier and a lake there shrank. How did this change life for the people living there?
opts: They had to find water and food in different places
They no longer needed any water or food
They found that food was easier to find near the lake
They stopped living in that part of Australia for ever
b.why: A drier climate shrank lakes and rivers, so water and food were found in different places. The card does not say that people always left the region, so that option goes too far.
b.clue: Think about where water and food are found when a lake shrinks.

a.best: They lived in Australia at the same time

b.best: They had to find water and food in different places

problems.detail: 'then died out as the climate dried' presents drying climate as the cause of extinction. The card says scientists still study why and look at evidence about both climate and people. The cause is genuinely debated, and human impact is a major hypothesis, so this line teaches a settled cause the card does not support.

'Both were in Australia for a long time, so people and these animals shared the land' uses faulty reasoning: being in Australia for a long time does not by itself show the two overlapped. Overlap is shown by evidence such as dated sites, not by both being long-lived.
The clue 'Look at the word alongside' points straight to the answer, so a student can pick the right option without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The remember line says megafauna died out because the climate dried, which contradicts the card's point that the cause is still studied (climate and people). The card's reasoning for overlap is weak, and the clue for question a gives the answer away.

proposal.title: Megafauna and changing climate
card: Megafauna means giant animals. Australia once had many, such as Diprotodon, a plant-eating marsupial about the size of a small car.
Scientists date fossils of megafauna and the places where people lived. These dates show that the first peoples and megafauna were in Australia at the same time.
Over thousands of years the climate became drier in many places. Lakes and rivers shrank, so people had to find water and food in different places.
Megafauna later died out. Historians and scientists still study why, and they look at evidence about climate change and about people.
proposal.remember: People and megafauna shared Australia, and the reasons megafauna died out are still being studied.

a.q: Which statement about Diprotodon and the first peoples of Australia is supported by evidence?
opts: They lived in Australia during the same period
Diprotodon died out before people reached Australia
Diprotodon was a meat-eater that hunted people
Scientists agree that people alone made it die out
a.why: Dated fossils and dated places where people lived show that the two were in Australia at the same time. Scientists do not agree on why megafauna died out. They still study evidence about both climate and people.
a.clue: What can dating fossils and old campsites tell us?

b.q: Over thousands of years, the climate in a region of Australia became drier and a lake there shrank. How did this change life for the people living there?
opts: They had to find water and food in different places
They no longer needed to look for water or food
They found that food was easier to find near the lake
They could stay in one place and never move for food
b.why: A drier climate shrank lakes and rivers, so people had to find water and food in different places. Staying in one place does not fit, because the water they relied on was disappearing.
b.clue: Think about what happens to a water source when a lake shrinks.
